text:
sam: FYI I'm opening a small docs PR to add a short "nftables vs iptables" migration note for the on-prem installer and a troubleshooting tip for HSM PKCS#11 permission errors during offline upgrades. Tagging @vikram for the nftables wording and @lina for HSM/PKCS11 specifics.

vikram: Ack. We should be explicit that some older distros use iptables-legacy while newer ones have nftables/iptables-nft. Quick recommendation: prefer nftables on hosts where possible and include the minimal compatibility commands to list translations.

lina: For HSMs the common gotcha is installer creating /var/lib/redwood/hsm as root:root with 0755 and PKCS11 middleware expecting group access. I'll add chown/chmod examples and a small check command.

sam: Draft wording below (will live under Private installer -> Networking & HSM Troubleshooting). Comments welcome.

sam: "nftables / iptables compatibility" snippet:
```bash
# Check which implementation is active
sudo update-alternatives --display iptables || true
# On systems with iptables-nft you can convert saved rules:
sudo iptables-restore-translate -f /etc/iptables/rules.v4 > /tmp/nft-rules.nft
# Apply test rule (non-destructive):
sudo nft -f /tmp/nft-rules.nft || echo "conversion failed, keep legacy rules"
```

vikram: LGTM. Maybe add one sentence about firewall manager tools (ufw/firewalld) that may re-write rules and require service restart.

lina: HSM PKCS11 permission checklist (airgapped/offline):
```bash
# Ensure installer-created dir and socket have correct ownership
sudo mkdir -p /var/lib/redwood/hsm
sudo chown -R root:redwoodhsm /var/lib/redwood/hsm
sudo chmod 0750 /var/lib/redwood/hsm
# If PKCS11 socket lives under /var/run/redwood, ensure group access
sudo chown -R root:redwoodhsm /var/run/redwood
sudo chmod 0770 /var/run/redwood
# Quick check: can redwoodsvc access the socket?
su -s /bin/bash -c 'test -w /var/run/redwood/kms.sock && echo OK || echo NOK' redwoodsvc
```

lina: Also note: some RPM-based airgapped installs don't provide semanage. Recommend adding fallback text: install policycoreutils-python-utils (RHEL) or policycoreutils (older) and a one-liner to `restorecon`.

secops-bot: Security note: document avoiding symlinked PKCS11 dirs, and advise verifying installer artifact checksums in offline flows. Add distro package names for semanage fallback and a small checksum verification example.

sam: Adding checksum snippet for offline verifier:
```bash
# Verify installer bundle on an airgapped host (example SHA256)
echo "<expected-sha256>  redwood-installer.tar.gz" > /tmp/checksum.txt
sha256sum -c /tmp/checksum.txt
# If missing sha256sum, `openssl dgst -sha256 redwood-installer.tar.gz` and compare visually
```

eng-ml: Minor: mention that some older HSM middleware (pkcs11-proxy) binds sockets under /run rather than /var/run, so add a short note to check both locations.

vikram: I'll add a one-line about firewalld/ufw interactions and note to restart after rule changes.

sam: I'll push a small PR with these snippets and brief bullets (migration, HSM checklist, checksum) and link it here. Planning to keep the section compact: <8 bullets + two code snippets.

docs-bot: CI queued for branch sam/nftables-hsm-checksum. Preview will be posted when ready.

sam: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4401 — please review for accuracy/security. Will wait for secops sign-off before merge.

lina: Quick nit: in the HSM example use group name `redwoodhsm` in docs but recommend admins map it to an existing group if they prefer. I'll add that line in the PR.

secops-bot: Security review scheduled; low-risk docs-only. Reminder: include steps to verify the HSM pkcs11 library checksum if vendors provide it.

vikram: Approved for technical accuracy (nft vs iptables). Left one small wording suggestion re: 'iptables-legacy' detection.

sam: Thanks all — will incorporate and merge after secops clears.
